projects.name: Solar + Energy Storage on Garage
projects.description: Install 5-7 solar panels on south-facing garage roof face (20x12 ft, ~2-2.8 kW) plus battery storage. Solar = standalone ROI investment (~5yr payback at $0.42/kWh). Battery = generator alternative (no lot space for generator). 30% federal ITC applies to both when paired.
projects.notes: DESIGN: South garage face only. 5 portrait panels = 2.0 kW; 7 mixed = 2.8 kW. ~3,200-4,500 kWh/yr production (20-26% offset). All-in after ITC: solar ~$9-10k, battery ~$9-10k. VENDORS: Sunergy (sunergy.com) — EnergySage 2026 CA Installer of Year, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door. NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com) — Diamond Certified, 35yr, San Mateo County, 40yr warranty. Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy) — online only. AVOID: Sunrun.

tasks.title: Analyze energy usage and size system
tasks.notes: 17,178 kWh/yr at $0.42/kWh avg. Target: 5-7 panels south garage face (20x12 ft) = 2-2.8 kW. ~5yr payback after ITC.

tasks.title: Research and shortlist solar installers
tasks.notes: Shortlist: Sunergy (sunergy.com, Enphase Platinum, no door-to-door), NRG Clean Power (nrgcleanpower.com, Diamond Certified, San Mateo County), Tesla Energy (tesla.com/energy, online only). Avoid Sunrun.

tasks.title: Contact installers for quotes
tasks.notes: Spec: south garage face (20x12 ft, 5-7 panels, ~2-2.8 kW), paired battery (Enphase IQ or Powerwall 3), detached garage sub-panel interconnect. Ask each for: $/W, panel brand, inverter type, battery spec, warranty, timeline, ITC total. Request free shade/LIDAR analysis.

tasks.title: Compare quotes and select installer
tasks.notes: Prefer Enphase microinverters over string inverter. Compare $/W, battery spec, warranty, timeline. 30% ITC on full system incl. battery.

tasks.title: Confirm ITC timing — credit files in year PTO is granted
tasks.notes: 30% federal ITC on Form 5695. Claimed in tax year Permission to Operate granted by PG&E. Battery qualifies only when solar-paired. Plan install timing accordingly.

insights.summary: The gradual decline from 26 to 21 connected devices paired with zero camera motion confirms the family is simply settling down for the weekday evening, with electronics entering sleep mode or moving into non-camera zones; this is a normal household pattern rather than a security concern.

The sustained presence of 21–26 mobile devices paired with zero camera motion on a weekday evening strongly indicates a large group of guests or a family gathering is settled indoors. This cross-signal pattern confirms the earlier correlation and suggests normal social activity, though verifying the guest count is advisable if unexpected.

The sustained presence of ~20 devices paired with zero camera motion strongly indicates that stationary IoT devices are being miscounted as mobile phones, or that the cameras are offline, rather than a large group of people being present. This matters because it points to a network configuration or camera system issue that could compromise accurate automation and security monitoring.

The sustained connection of ~20 devices paired with zero camera motion on a weekday afternoon strongly suggests the house is unoccupied with phones charging, or the presence system is falsely registering stationary IoT devices as people. This cross-signal mismatch indicates a likely sensor calibration issue or an empty home that warrants quick verification.

The sustained presence of 19–21 devices far exceeds the family’s typical footprint, but the complete lack of camera motion indicates the activity is likely confined to a camera-blind zone or consists of stationary IoT devices rather than active people. This warrants a quick check to confirm whether it’s a quiet guest gathering in an unmonitored area or a network artifact.

The sustained presence of 19-22 mobile devices combined with zero camera motion during a weekday afternoon strongly suggests a large group of unregistered guests is gathered in camera-blind areas, warranting a security or guest management check.

The sustained 18–22 device count paired with zero camera motion during a weekday midday strongly indicates either a large indoor gathering or network/IoT devices being misclassified as phones; verifying camera status and device types will clarify whether this is a false positive or an unlogged event.

The sustained 18-20 device count paired with zero camera activity indicates unregistered guests or devices are passively occupying the home, likely in camera blind spots; the dip to 18 at 13:14 suggests a device may have left or dropped signal, warranting a quick check.

The sustained count of 19-21 mobile devices during a weekday midday strongly suggests unregistered guests or contractors are present, as Miller and Penelope are likely at school; the rapid oscillation indicates frequent network connections or band-switching, warranting a quick verification of who is in the house.

The connected device count (17-22) is unusually high for a household of four, and the rapid oscillation suggests either a morning IoT sync cycle or network polling instability rather than actual human presence. This warrants a quick network check to ensure no unauthorized connections or false-positive detections are skewing your presence automations.
